title: Trump: Energy Department bans use of terms, "climate change," "emissions"
description_short: Trump: Energy Department bans use of terms, "climate change," "emissions"
description_medium: On September 26, 2025, the Energy Department’s Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy told staff to avoid terms including “climate change,” “clean energy,” “sustainability” and “decarbonization” in internal and public communications. The linked account says the email cited alignment with administration priorities rather than a scientific reason; it does not document effects on research or programs.
description_long: The Energy Department’s Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy sent staff an email on September 26, 2025, adding climate-related and energy terms to a “list of words to avoid.” The examples included “climate change,” “energy transition,” “sustainability,” “clean energy,” “carbon/CO2 footprint,” “green” and “decarbonization,” along with language about tax credits and subsidies. The TrumpFile timeline says the instruction covered both internal and public communications and that no scientific reason was offered; instead, the email reportedly said the terms did not align with the administration’s “perspectives and priorities.” The source documents an office communication directing staff away from certain language. It does not show that a formal regulation or department-wide legal ban was issued, or identify research papers, grants or public materials that were changed as a result. The action affected the vocabulary staff were asked to use when communicating about energy and climate topics. The title’s broader “bans” wording should be read in light of the source’s description of an email and a list of terms to avoid.
subcategory: Energy Department communications guidance on climate terminology
organization_tags: Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy

title: Trump: White House slams Nobel Committee over Trump loss
description_short: Trump: White House slams Nobel Committee over Trump loss
description_medium: After Venezuelan activist María Corina Machado received the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize, White House communications director Steven Cheung criticized the Nobel Committee on X. Cheung said the committee placed politics over peace and praised Trump’s claimed role in ending wars. The linked account says Trump had publicly campaigned for the prize, but records a response to the award announcement rather than any influence on the committee.
description_long: Donald Trump had publicly expressed a desire to receive the Nobel Peace Prize in the weeks before the 2025 award, saying he deserved recognition for ending global conflicts. When the Nobel Committee announced Venezuelan activist María Corina Machado as the recipient, White House communications director Steven Cheung criticized the committee in a post on X. He wrote that it had put “politics over peace” and said Trump would continue making peace deals, ending wars and saving lives. The linked TrumpFile page documents a White House spokesperson’s reaction to the award and the administration’s argument for Trump’s recognition. It does not show that the committee changed its decision, that the White House took action against the organization, or that Trump’s comments affected the award process. The incident was a public complaint following Machado’s selection, not an official finding about the Nobel Committee’s conduct. Keeping Cheung’s statement attributed distinguishes the White House’s criticism from an independently established judgment about the prize.
subcategory: White House response to 2025 Nobel Peace Prize decision

title: Trump's NASA closes top research library
description_short: Trump's NASA closes top research library
description_medium: NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center library closed on January 2, 2026, after in-person services had ended on December 9. NASA administrator Jared Isaacman described the change as consolidation, but Goddard employees reported disrupted digital access and unavailable journals. The linked page says physical materials were not fully digitized and that the 2022 facilities plan did not call for the library’s full closure.
description_long: NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center, home to the agency’s largest library, closed on January 2, 2026, after in-person library services—including book checkouts—had stopped on December 9. NASA administrator Jared Isaacman described the closure as part of a consolidation plan under which physical and digital resources would remain available. Goddard employees told the linked account that researchers were already having trouble reaching online journals and the Space Science Data Coordinated Archive; much of the library’s print collection had not been digitized. A scientist said losing library services would slow research and make work less convenient. The article also notes that a 2022 facilities plan contemplated replacing some buildings but did not call for fully closing the library, and that specialized spacecraft-testing equipment was discarded. Employees and their union said shutdown conditions accelerated the closure before replacement facilities were underway. The account therefore describes more than a change of address: it reports reduced access to research material and equipment, while distinguishing those reports from NASA’s claim that consolidation would preserve access.
subcategory: NASA Goddard research library and facility closures

title: Trump: FCC approves illegal acquisition of TEGNA by Nexstar in big blow to local media
description_short: Trump: FCC approves illegal acquisition of TEGNA by Nexstar in big blow to local media
description_medium: The FCC and Justice Department approved Nexstar’s acquisition of TEGNA on March 19, 2026. TrumpFile says the combined company would reach 54.5% of U.S. television households and control 259 stations after divesting six. Eight states sued, arguing the deal violated federal ownership limits; the linked page does not establish a final court ruling that the acquisition was illegal.
description_long: The Federal Communications Commission and Justice Department approved Nexstar’s acquisition of TEGNA on March 19, 2026. The linked TrumpFile timeline says the combined company would own 259 television stations and reach 54.5% of U.S. households, after agreeing to divest six stations. In Denver, the deal added TEGNA stations including 9NEWS KUSA and KTVD to Nexstar’s existing KDVR and KWGN holdings; CEO Perry Sook said some operations would be combined. Eight states filed suit to challenge the merger. The timeline says the states argued that the acquisition exceeded a federal limit of 39% household reach and quotes Colorado Attorney General Phil Weiser warning that fewer owners could mean less diversity of voices, higher consumer costs and newsroom job losses. Those effects are predictions and legal objections, not findings that the merger was unlawful or that those outcomes had already occurred. The linked material records regulatory approval and the states’ challenge but does not provide a final judicial ruling. Because the headline calls the acquisition “illegal,” the legal conclusion remains unresolved in the supplied source. A corrected title should describe approval and the pending challenge rather than state illegality as settled.
subcategory: FCC approval and state challenge to local broadcast consolidation

title: Trump Weighs His Options in Carrying Out New Strikes in Iran
description_short: Trump Weighs His Options in Carrying Out New Strikes in Iran
